preconditions: Owned temporary model/profile files and Work roots; real native model, graph, SRX, checkpoint and transaction paths. In-process tests use an explicitly labelled recorded-build fixture; process tests build and run the actual module/zipapp. Trusted host registry, initial binding and normative publication authority are explicit test harness inputs.

The host-boundary case uses actual newly built module execution and native RLIMIT_NOFILE changes in independent owned child processes; low-limit failure is a real EMFILE, not an invented softbudget refusal.
steps: Build the actual core module tree and zipapp and invoke their trusted host evaluation adapter in independent isolated Python processes with no PATH discovery.
Move runtime, Work and protected project roots between invocations, remove original captured source files and alternate resource profiles; resume from durable bytes.
Verify exact final native results and reject an incompatible build before a writing lease.

Check rehashed incomplete/contradictory retained data and actual changed input/runtime/host prerequisites; retain the actual checkpoint and all required observations, then resume only after a compatible prerequisite is restored.

oracle.scope: Actual built module and zipapp executions continue in fresh processes after inode-preserving path changes and original source loss, without an in-memory prior session. Missing/empty/corrupt caches and incompatible builds are checked. This is current-host evidence, not the entire release portability matrix. These are consistency and current-host behavior checks, not authentication, bounded-memory completion or full release portability approval.
